card.title: 169. GRENADIERS
card.text: The enemy discards a card at random after giving an order.
card.flavorText: The 169th Grenadier Regiment was part of the 68th Infantry Division, a German unit formed in Guben on August 26, 1939. It became operational in time for the invasion of Poland, crossing from German-held territory into southern Poland and advancing through Sandomierz and Janów. After the campaign ended, the division served as an occupation force in Poland until November. In early 1940, it was moved west to Germany near Trier, and later took part in the invasion of France. During the second phase of that campaign, it advanced from the Sedan region into eastern France, reaching Épinal, before being sent back east. By mid-1940, the division was stationed in occupied Poland for border security. It joined Operation Barbarossa on June 22, 1941, advancing from southeastern Poland into the Soviet Union as part of Army Group South. It pushed through western Ukraine, passing Lviv and Vinnytsia, and reached the outskirts of Cherkasy in central Ukraine. In late 1941 it advanced to Poltava and Kharkiv in eastern Ukraine, where it endured harsh winter fighting until early 1942. In summer, it reached Voronezh in western Russia, but had to withdraw in 1943 through areas like the Oskol River and Sumy in northeastern Ukraine. After heavy losses, it was reconstituted in Poland and returned to the front in 1944, fighting in western Ukraine near Lviv. The division then retreated across the Carpathian Mountains into southern Poland, later pulling back into Upper Silesia and finally into Moravia, present-day Czech Republic, where it surrendered to Soviet forces in 1945.
